Rule. Hold this rule for Strategy: Swap a whole algorithm behind one interface without editing the caller. Say it before you pick a tool from Design patterns.

Why it matters. Interviewers on the Design patterns track listen for whether you can name the idea strategy and refuse the common wrong pick. When to use. Use Strategy when the prompt's access pattern or force matches the summary above, when a prior slug in its after-list is already in hand, and when saying the rule changes which next step you take.

When to refuse. Refuse Strategy when a simpler tool already covers the force, when a prerequisite in after is still missing, or when applying it would invent a mechanism the track never taught. Prefer naming the missing slug over bluffing.
